details.description: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B is a 70-billion-parameter dense reasoning model that DeepSeek created by fine-tuning Meta's Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct on roughly 800,000 reasoning traces generated by the full DeepSeek-R1 model, released in January 2025 alongside DeepSeek-R1 itself. It carries R1's step-by-step 'thinking' style of reasoning for math, coding and logic tasks into a smaller, dense architecture. Fireworks AI serves it with a 131,000-token context length. It is released under the MIT license, layered on Meta's Llama 3.3 license for the underlying weights.
advantages: Scores 70.0% pass@1 on AIME 2024, per DeepSeek's Hugging Face model card.
Scores 94.5% pass@1 on MATH-500, per DeepSeek's Hugging Face model card.
Scores 65.2% pass@1 on GPQA Diamond, per DeepSeek's Hugging Face model card.
Scores 57.5% pass@1 on LiveCodeBench, per DeepSeek's Hugging Face model card.
disadvantages: DeepSeek's model card recommends capping output around 32,768 tokens and notes the model can 'bypass thinking pattern' on some queries, which may reduce answer quality.
DeepSeek recommends against using a system prompt, with all instructions placed in the user turn instead.

DeepSeek's own API changelog labels this reasoning generation 'legacy R1' and discontinued the deepseek-reasoner model id in favor of the DeepSeek-V4 series by July 2026, though the open weights stay available on Hugging Face and via third-party hosts such as Fireworks AI.
use_cases: Complex multi-step reasoning and logic tasks
General text generation with an explicit chain-of-thought 'thinking' step

notes: DeepSeek's model card recommends a maximum generation length of 32,768 tokens for reliable output, well below the 131,072-token max_input/max_output in the catalog facts and the 131,000-token context Fireworks advertises; the catalog's larger figures are kept as authoritative per instructions, but users should know the maker's own tested/recommended length is much shorter. Exact parameter count is reported inconsistently across sources (Hugging Face 'Model size 71B params', Fireworks '70.5 billion') so the description rounds to 70 billion. The model card's 'outperforms OpenAI-o1-mini across various benchmarks' line is stated only about the sibling DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B, not this 70B checkpoint, so that advantage was removed rather than misattributed; the card also gives no exact release day, and Hugging Face's repo metadata shows this checkpoint was published 2025-01-20, so the description was softened to 'January 2025'. DeepSeek's own API changelog (api-docs.deepseek.com/updates) shows deepseek-reasoner moved on from DeepSeek-R1 to DeepSeek-V3.1/V3.2-Exp in 2025 and then to the V4 series by mid-2026, referring to this generation as 'legacy R1'.
